# SEO-034: Provide a single meta description per indexable page

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `metadata` |
| Category | `SEARCH_DISCOVERABILITY` |
| Minimum level | `LITE` |
| Severity | `MEDIUM` |
| Impact | `LOW` |
| Change safety | `SAFE_AUTOMATIC` |
| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `MEDIUM` |

## Statement

Each indexable page carries at most one meta description element, and where present its content describes that specific page rather than repeating a site-wide sentence across every route.

## Rationale

A description that is present and page-specific gives the engine a candidate snippet drawn from the page's own subject; a site-wide sentence gives it nothing to prefer over text it extracts from the body itself.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Set the description where the route already knows its own subject - the page module, the content record, or the CMS field - rather than in a shared layout default. Where no page-specific text exists, omit the element instead of emitting a generic one.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Collect the description meta content from the served response across a route sample and count how many distinct values appear.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: `meta-description-single`

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: Search engines frequently generate their own snippet in place of the supplied description, so this control makes a page-specific candidate available; it does not determine what is displayed.
